audit.why: TRICKY 7.5/10 matches 47.94% over 705 games and a level chart that reads Olaf for stages 1-6.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 spike and the mid block both describe Ragnarok as a blanket CC immunity and tell the player to 'play aggressively for those 45 seconds' when it is down.
audit.why: Riot's description says Olaf is immune to disables only for as long as he keeps attacking — stop feeding him a target and the immunity ends. And Ragnarok's cooldown is 100/90/80, not 45; the player is told to expect a window less than half the real length and will stop respecting it far too early.
audit.corrected: Real 100-second rank-1 cooldown and the keeps-attacking condition written into the spike, mid and whys[4].
sources: champ-data/_kits/olaf.json (R Ragnarok, cd 100/90/80, 'immune to disables for as long as he keeps attacking')

audit.whatIsWrong: Three fabricated mechanics, each repeated. (a) Undertow is said to ROOT — 'axes root', 'root you in place' — in early, whys[2] and wants.foe[0]. (b) Tough It Out is called 'W lifesteal', 'W regeneration' and 'his W heals back whatever Q damage you land'. (c) Reckless Swing is given a 9-second cooldown at level 2.
audit.why: (a) Undertow slows and shreds armour; it has no root, so the whole 'rooted then Reckless Swing' pattern the page teaches you to fear does not exist and the player will play the wrong spacing. (b) Tough It Out is an attack speed buff and a SHIELD — no healing at all, which also undercuts the 'anti-heal stays core' build advice. (c) Reckless Swing is 11 seconds at rank 1, not 9; two extra seconds is a whole extra Flamespitter.
audit.corrected: Slow replaces root everywhere, shield replaces lifesteal, and 11s replaces 9s.
sources: champ-data/_kits/olaf.json (Q Undertow: slow + armour shred, no root; W Tough It Out: attack speed + shield, cd 16/15/14/13/12; E Reckless Swing, cd 11/10/9/8/7)

audit.whatIsWrong: Undertow's axe pickup reset is never mentioned.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'If Olaf picks up the axe, the ability's cooldown is reset.' That single line is the lane's real spacing rule — retreat AWAY from the landed axe and his 9-second slow stays on cooldown; walk over it and he re-throws immediately. Nothing on the page told the player this.
audit.corrected: Added to wants.foe[0] and the cooldown breakdown.
sources: champ-data/_kits/olaf.json (Q Undertow, cd 9, pickup resets cooldown)

audit.whatIsWrong: No real cooldown numbers anywhere, and the one number given (45 seconds for Ragnarok) is invented.
audit.why: Ragnarok 100s, Undertow 9s with a pickup reset and Reckless Swing 11s are the three clocks that decide every trade.
audit.corrected: All three written into the cooldown breakdown and the Do entry.

edits.before: At level 1 Olaf is already dangerous — his thrown axes apply a slow and his kit wants nothing more than to root you in place and land Reckless Swing before you can Q-and-walk-away. Do not stand in axe range to harass; poke with Electro-Harpoon from safe distance and accept that Flamespitter Q trades level 1 are a coin flip you do not need to take. At level 2 Olaf's E true damage comes online and your Scrap Shield stops doing the work you want — he can shield-ignore chip you every 9 seconds. By level 3 the full kit is live on both sides but Olaf's pattern is strictly better: he throws an axe to root, Reckless Swings through your shield, and his W heals back whatever Q damage you land. Farm safely, keep your Heat in the Danger Zone so you have an empowered W ready if he dives you, and do not waste double-harpoon trying to trade — use it to escape the stick.
edits.after: At level 1 Olaf is already dangerous — Undertow slows and shreds armour, it does not root, and he wants to stick to you long enough to land Reckless Swing before you Q-and-walk-away. Do not stand in axe range to harass; poke with Electro-Harpoon from safe distance and accept that Flamespitter Q trades level 1 are a coin flip you do not need to take. At level 2 Olaf's E true damage comes online and your Scrap Shield stops doing the work you want — he can shield-ignore chip you every 11 seconds at rank 1. By level 3 the full kit is live on both sides but Olaf's pattern is strictly better: he throws an axe to slow, Reckless Swings through your shield, and Tough It Out shields off whatever Q damage you land. Farm safely, keep your Heat in the Danger Zone so you have an empowered W ready if he dives you, and do not waste double-harpoon trying to trade — use it to escape the stick.

edits.after: Olaf's axes and his Tough It Out shield let him win extended trades you try to force with Flamespitter — your DoT cannot chew through a shield he refreshes every 16 seconds.

edits.before: Ragnarok makes Olaf CC-immune and strips your only real dueling edge — your Scrap Shield's movement speed and Electro-Harpoon slow are both irrelevant while he presses R.
edits.after: Ragnarok makes Olaf immune to disables only while he keeps attacking, and it is a 100-second cooldown at rank 1 — break off and the immunity lapses, so your Harpoon slow bites again.

edits.before: Levels 4 through 6 are his lane. Experienced Heat cycling does not fix the fundamental problem: Reckless Swing true damage bypasses your only defensive tool and Olaf's W lifesteal sustains through the DoT you deal back. Short trades are still your least-bad option — Danger Zone Q into immediate Scrap Shield and back off — but extended fights where you stand in each other's faces are concessions you lose. At 6 Ragnarok is the match-defining threat: when he presses it, Electro-Harpoon's slow and Scrap Shield's movement speed become decorative. If Ragnarok is down, that is your all-in window; play aggressively for those 45 seconds. Equalizer at 6 is your escape hatch — if he forces a bad trade, R across your own feet to slow him and disengage under tower.
edits.after: Levels 4 through 6 are his lane. Experienced Heat cycling does not fix the fundamental problem: Reckless Swing true damage bypasses your only defensive tool and Tough It Out shields off the DoT you deal back. Short trades are still your least-bad option — Danger Zone Q into immediate Scrap Shield and back off — but extended fights where you stand in each other's faces are concessions you lose. At 6 Ragnarok is the match-defining threat: when he presses it, Electro-Harpoon's slow and Scrap Shield's movement speed become decorative. Ragnarok is 100 seconds at rank 1 and only holds while he keeps swinging, so break contact to end it and all-in inside that cooldown. Equalizer at 6 is your escape hatch — if he forces a bad trade, R across your own feet to slow him and disengage under tower.

notes: The full layer says 'anti-heal stays core' in breakdown.late and tldr/winCon lead with 'Anti-heal'. Olaf's kit contains no healing — Tough It Out is a shield and Berserker Rage is attack speed — so anti-heal is only justified by his item build (Sundered Sky / Death's Dance), not by the matchup. Worth the user reconsidering that build line; I left it alone because I cannot verify his current top-lane item trend from local data. Ragnarok's exact interaction with slows (as opposed to disables) is not in the kit file, so I wrote 'disables' as Riot words it and made no claim about slows being cleansed — note that the existing don't-entry title 'E-slow during his R (cleansed)' asserts more than the data supports.
